panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of real patient in article focused on scalp nevocellular nevus, with caption and in-text describing hyperpigmented hair-bearing lesions on back/thighs. Lesions are visibly pigmented raised oval lesions consistent with pigmented nevus papules, supporting acquired_melanocytic_nevus attribution per title and caption. Size 2-6 cm is larger than classic common mole, so variant.
panels.attribution_text: AlBurshaid et al. Multiple stage tissue expansion for reconstruction of scalp nevocellular nevus in pediatric age group.. GMS Interdisciplinary plastic and reconstructive surgery DGPW 2019. doi:10.3205/iprs000134. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Hyperpigmented lesions, 4 on the back and 2 on the thighs with different sizes. All lesions were full of hair and weren’t secreting any discharge.
in_text_mentions: Local examination revealed a pigmented, thick, and corrugated lesion that involved almost her entire scalp leaving a strip of normal skin with a width of 10 cm (Figure 2 (Fig. 2)). On full body examination, she was found to have scattered, hyper-pigmented lesions fully covered with hair on the lower back and the upper thighs with estimated sizes ranging from 2x 2 to 6x 6 cm (Figure 3 (Fig. 3)).
